decision.explanation: The provided evidence (pmid-27093365) exclusively concerns Merkel-cell carcinoma, not cutaneous adenocystic carcinoma. The study reports that PD-L1 expression did not correlate with response to pembrolizumab in Merkel-cell carcinoma. There is no evidence in the supplied material regarding CD274 expression, immune checkpoint inhibitor sensitivity, or any other predictive biomarker status in cutaneous adenocystic carcinoma. Therefore, the evidence is insufficient to support the claim for the target disease.

citations.quote: Eligible patients were at least 18 years old and had distant metastatic or recurrent locoregional Merkel-cell carcinoma . . . Samples were considered to be positive for PD-L1 if 1% or more of tumor cells expressed PD-L1. . . . In our analysis of tumors from 25 patients, neither PD-L1 expression on tumor cells (Fig. 4C) nor expression on infiltrating immune cells (not shown) correlated significantly with clinical response to pembrolizumab.
